definition: Sign tracking is a tendency, identified in a computerized Pavlovian conditioned approach task, to respond in a way that distinguishes a person from a goal-tracker. In this source, stronger sign-tracking tendencies are discussed as being positively associated with alcohol-related attentional bias and linked with higher alcohol use.
